svg.title: For the actual interpolant, take the surrounding right-closed mesh cube. If θa is the coordinate fraction measured from its right endpoint, assign a vertex choosing the left endpoint in coordinates I the weight Q Q a∈I θa a/∈I(1 −θa). These weights are nonnegative and sum to one. Every vertex is within O(naN) of the physical point. Cluster convergence at those vertices, continuity of the limit and compactness imply uniformly small vertex errors on each compact collision-free set. The error of their weighted sum is bounded by the maximum vertex error. Thus the multilinear interpolants converge locally uniformly, also at cell ties. This assertion does not require or claim that a finite- mesh interpolant is smooth at its cell boundaries; lattice differences are taken before interpolation.
